question: Which state of India has the highest population density as per 2011 census?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihar has the highest population density in India as per the 2011 Census.
 
• The population density of Bihar is 1,106 persons per square kilometer, which is significantly higher than the national average of 382 persons per square kilometer.
 
• This high population density is attributed to the state's high fertility rate and relatively small geographical area.
 
• Other states with high population density include West Bengal and Kerala, but they lag behind Bihar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density**

 
 
• Population density is a measurement of population per unit area or unit volume.
 
• It is often represented as people per square kilometer or people per square mile.
 
• This metric is used to understand the distribution of population in a specific area and is crucial for urban planning and resource allocation.
 
 
 
• **2011 Census**
 
 
• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National census since 1871 and was conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The census provides comprehensive data on the demographic, social, and economic profile of India.
 
• It includes information on population size, density, distribution, and various other factors such as literacy rates, employment status, and household amenities.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Population Density**
 
 
• Several factors influence population density, including geographical area, fertility rates, mortality rates, migration patterns, and government policies.
 
• Areas with favorable living conditions, job opportunities, and better infrastructure tend to have higher population densities.
 
• Conversely, regions with harsh climates, lack of resources, and limited economic opportunities typically have lower population densities.
 
 
 
• **Implications of High Population Density**
 
 
• High population density can lead to various challenges such as overcrowding, strain on infrastructure and resources, and environmental degradation.
 
• It can also result in increased competition for jobs, housing, and services.
 
• On the positive side, high population density can foster economic growth, cultural exchange, and innovation due to the concentration of people and activities.
